provenance.construction: Cyclic generalized bicycle at m=233, a prime with ord_2(m)=29, so the nontrivial cyclotomic cosets of 2 all have size 29. The divisor g is one such coset's minimal polynomial, of degree 29, which fixes k = 2 deg g = 58 by construction. The pair (a,b) was then drawn from the ideal (g) by information-set decoding over sparse supports, keeping weights 7 and 9; both are odd, so x+1 does not divide the gcd and no weight-m block logical is forced. H_X = [circ(a) | circ(b)] and H_Z = [circ(b)^T | circ(a)^T] on n = 2m = 466 qubits at uniform row weight 16, with a = [14, 21, 47, 74, 115, 129, 142] and b = [14, 29, 32, 69, 97, 118, 147, 183, 187].
provenance.notes: Distance is an upper bound from the lighter of two witnesses, weight 52 on X and 56 on Z, both carried in this file. A 24-seed randomized information-set search at 2,000,000 trials per seed spread 52 to 60 with the minimum found by one seed. A single run of 8,000,000 trials, matching the verifier's own depth, reads 56. A search restricted to logicals supported inside one circulant block, which a general search is blind to, found nothing below 64. Folding onto the x^t-invariant subspaces leaves a lightest surviving logical of weight 176. The design point is deg g / m = 0.124.
